title: Israel Strikes Choueifat Neighborhood in Beirut's Southern Suburbs Ahead of Washington Talks; 11+ Killed
detail: Israel's air force struck the Choueifat neighborhood in Beirut's southern suburbs on May 28 — close to Beirut International Airport — the day before crucial Lebanon-Israel peace negotiations in Washington. White smoke billowed from a struck residential building; the specific target was not immediately clarified by the IDF. Earlier on May 28, Israeli strikes across southern Lebanon killed at least 11 people including two children and wounded 21 more. A drone struck an apartment building housing displaced families in Sidon, killing five people and wounding 21, including five children. Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam publicly condemned Israel's 'onslaughts' on Tyre and Nabatieh, calling the ongoing displacement 'collective punishment,' on the eve of the Washington negotiations. Lebanon's stated negotiating priorities included securing a real ceasefire, a timetable for Israeli withdrawal, and release of Lebanese prisoners held by Israel.

media.caption: Israel strikes Beirut suburb as Lebanon-Israel peace talks approach — Washington Post

title: UN Warns Israeli Bombing Puts Tyre UNESCO World Heritage Site 'in Serious Danger'
detail: UN officials warned on May 28 that Israeli bombings are putting the ancient ruins of Tyre (Sur), a UNESCO World Heritage Site, 'in serious danger' due to strikes falling very close to the site. Tyre's ancient ruins — including Roman hippodrome, necropolis, and Phoenician remains — have been on the UNESCO World Heritage list since 1984. The UN Security Council's Lebanon monitoring report raised alarm as Israel continued to issue evacuation orders for the city and conduct strikes in its vicinity. The Tyre ruins represent one of the best-preserved examples of ancient Levantine civilization and are irreplaceable. UNESCO Director-General called for all parties to respect protections for cultural heritage under international humanitarian law.

media.caption: UN warns Israeli bombardment puts Tyre's UNESCO World Heritage ruins at serious risk — Security Council Report
